commentary.summary: This money-leak review for the business owner highlights key areas where money is being lost. The most important is the losing months calculation with net_profit of -14120 and -14740. What is happening is net losses in those periods. Likely cause is rising expenses against lower revenue. Step-by-step fix: review all expenses in those periods, cut non-essential ones like certain vendor_spend, then adjust pricing and sales. Prevent by monthly budget reviews and forecasting. Next is overdue invoices with value 15415 from multiple invoice_contract where invoice_paid is 0. Likely cause is missing follow-up processes. Fix: contact each customer, send reminders, enforce terms. Prevent with upfront deposits. Other leaks like overtime, labor utilization, card processing fees, fuel, callbacks, unprofitable jobs and rising recurring charges follow similar patterns of inefficiency and require targeted fixes. One potential additional way money is lost not captured in calculations is large vendor_spend on certain dates.

facts.text: Losing months calculation shows net_profit of -14120 for period 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-30 and -14740 for period 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-31.
Overdue invoices calculation shows value 15415 from multiple invoice_contract with invoice_paid of 0.
Overtime calculation shows value 5614.25 with overtime_cost values such as 1026, 1254, 1140, 1368, 1083 and 1197.
Labor utilization calculation for Jake Lindgren and Marcus Olson shows value 5529.35 with varying hours values.
Card processing fees calculation shows value 3744.54 with fees values such as 1766.93, 1906.03, 2076.6.
Fuel calculation shows value 3110 while revenue was 103800, 112200, 122500 then 75700, 95900, 100500.
Possible duplicate charges hypothesis shows value 3030.85 with repeated vendor_spend of 612.48 and 2418.37.
Rising recurring charges calculation shows value 300 with vendor_spend rising from 149 to 249.

patterns.text: Multiple periods show job_revenue lower than job_labor plus job_materials for the same jobs.
Software subscription expenses and fuel expenses both trend upward across the full period.
Several invoice_contract have corresponding invoice_paid of 0 in the same periods.
Vendor_spend records show repeated identical values on nearby dates and overlapping subscriptions.

hypotheses.text: Net losses in the two months are caused by rising expenses in multiple categories outpacing revenue.
alternatives: One-time unrecorded costs in those specific months
Seasonal demand drop not captured in data

hypotheses.text: Overdue invoices with value 15415 result from lack of systematic follow-up after sending invoice_contract.
alternatives: Customer disputes over job quality or pricing

hypotheses.text: Overtime and low labor utilization stem from inefficient scheduling of jobs to available technicians.
alternatives: Unexpected urgent callbacks requiring extra hours

hypotheses.text: Card processing fees exceed target due to payment mix or processor rates not optimized.
alternatives: High volume of certain card types from customers

hypotheses.text: Large vendor_spend on 2026-09-19 and 2026-09-05 may indicate additional money leaks missed by calculations. Insufficient data to determine this reliably.
alternatives: These are valid job-related costs already reflected in other records

recommendations.text: Contact customers for all past due invoices immediately and set up automated reminders to collect the value 15415 faster.
Review all expenses during the periods with net_profit of -14120 and -14740 then reduce recurring ones to stop future losses.
Improve job scheduling to cut overtime_cost and raise billable hours for Jake Lindgren and Marcus Olson.
Shop for new card processors or negotiate rates to bring fees down from the current level.
Audit and cancel overlapping subscriptions such as QUICKFLEET GPS MONTHLY and FLEETTRACK PRO GPS to avoid duplicate payments.
Create and follow a job pricing guide to prevent underpriced jobs and ensure revenue covers labor and materials.
Monitor fuel expenses per job and optimize routes or equipment to control costs that rose over the period.
Verify every vendor_spend against invoices and job records to eliminate any duplicate charges going forward.

additionalDataNeeded: Itemized descriptions and purposes for all large vendor_spend entries
Customer communication logs for overdue invoices
Detailed job assignment and scheduling records
Breakdown of what each payroll_cost and overtime_cost covers per technician
limitations: Several calculations are classified as estimates rather than deterministic.
All source data is owner entered and may contain entry errors.
No causal data or notes explaining why losses or inefficiencies occurred.
Limited periods covered prevent seeing longer-term trends reliably.
questionsForOwner: What specific events or costs led to the net losses in those two months?
What is the current process for following up on unpaid invoices?
How are jobs assigned to technicians like Jake Lindgren and Marcus Olson?
Are there any unlisted reasons for the repeated vendor charges seen in the data?
